items.title: Introduction
items.body:
Status: approved · Revision: 9 · Describes `main`

This document shows hoop's components and how they interact. Code-level detail belongs in the LLD. Diagrams are written in Mermaid. The design text points only to requirements, by their IDs.

items.title: Context and scope
items.body:
The hoop package is a Node.js (TypeScript) package with one process per agent session: `hoop mcp` speaks MCP over stdio to the agent. Reviews live as JSON files on the machine. Team reviews live in a GitHub PR on the reviewed repository. The review pages run on 127.0.0.1 in one background pages process (FR-49). Sessions and commands start it when nothing answers, and it outlives them.

Three outside parties take part besides the agent and the browser. GitHub signs a person in for the final approval (FR-83). Claude Code runs a hook when an agent leaves plan mode (FR-87). GitHub Actions runs the checks on every pull request (FR-122). devloop lives in this repository and holds the document templates, review standards and the writing checker (FR-99 to FR-117). The goals and the scope are the PRD's sections 1 and 5.

```mermaid flowchart LR   agent[Author agent] -->|MCP over stdio| mcp[hoop mcp session]   person[Reviewer and requester] -->|browser on this machine| pages[Pages process 127.0.0.1:4747]   pages -->|device sign-in over HTTPS| gh[GitHub]   mcp -->|gh api| pr[Decision PR on GitHub]   mcp --> store[(Review store ~/.hoop)]   pages --> store   mcp -->|reads and writes| repo[(Repository files)]   pages -->|reads| repo   mcp -->|runs the allowed check| check[Project's check command]   cc[Claude Code] -->|plan mode hook| hook[Plan review hook]   hook -->|hoop plan-review| store   contributor[Contributor] -->|push| ci[GitHub Actions]   cmds[hoop wait, hoop audit, hoop serve] --> store ```

items.title: Assumptions and constraints
items.body:
- Node 18.18 is the floor, and hoop adds no native module. So the store is JSON files, not SQLite.
- The pages fetch nothing from another host. Every file a page loads comes from the pages process.
- The system can't tell an agent's request from a person's by the request alone. Both reach the   same local address. So only a GitHub sign-in held by the browser marks a person.
- The project registers one GitHub OAuth App with the device flow on. The device flow needs only   its public client ID, which ships with hoop.
- MCP clients end a call after 60 seconds, so a tool that waits returns before that.
- Claude Code lets a hook stop a tool call and give the agent a reason. The plan hook uses that.
- An MCP tool list is fixed for a session, so a session reads its project's settings once.
- Stored reviews, trackers and changes made by any earlier hoop must keep working (NFR-9, FR-142).
- Every PRD, HLD and LLD names its kind in its title, as the templates show. A document whose title   names no kind is checked as a plain document.
- On submit, hoop gives the checker a temporary copy of the document and runs it in the   repository's folder. So the checker learns the kind from the text, and finds the project's list   from that folder.
- The writing checker stays one standalone script that runs with python3 alone. It ships inside   devloop and must run in any project that uses devloop.

items.title: Architecture
items.body:
| Component | Files | Responsibility | Talks to (how) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract | `src/contract.ts` | It holds the schemas for review and feedback documents, anchors, scopes and validation. It gives each heading's section, with every section nested in it. | Every component imports it. |
| Edit engine | `src/edit.ts` | It locates a span, writes it into the one field it came from, and counts words. It holds one table of every edit rule, by name. | The materializer and the core, in process. |
| Markdown | `src/markdown.ts` | It turns any markdown into a review document and back, and records each source line's place. | The core, in process. |
| Section matcher | `src/markdown.ts` | It keeps a section's ID across revisions, by heading and then by place. | The markdown parser, in process. |
| Rendering | `src/render.ts` | It writes the line-numbered `.md` for a GitHub review and the PR description's checkboxes. | The GitHub component, in process. |
| Store | `src/store.ts` | It keeps reviews, revisions, feedback, replies, proposals, applied edits and check outcomes as JSON files. | The file system under the hoop folder. |
| Core | `src/hoop.ts` | It receives every operation and coordinates the components below. It resolves quotes to lines and states each submit's outcome. | Every component below, in process. |
| Review rules | `src/rules.ts` | They decide whether a review can change, find a comment thread, and give each review its status key. They also decide whose verdict a verdict is. | The core and the sign-in service. |
| Quote resolver | `src/quote.ts` | It finds the one line that holds quoted words, or names every place they occur. | The core, in process. |
| Materializer | `src/materialize.ts` | It turns suggestions and accepted edits into new revisions. | The edit engine and the store. |
| GitHub | `src/github.ts` | It opens and revises decision PRs, syncs their reviews and replies, all through `gh api`. | GitHub, through the `gh` command. |
| Operations | `src/ops.ts` | It defines every operation once, marks each one as core or devloop, and holds the old names as aliases. | The MCP server and the CLI read it. |
| Project settings | `src/project.ts` | It decides whether a project has devloop, from the project's config or its change folders. | The MCP server reads it when the session starts. |
| MCP server | `src/mcp.ts` | It lists the core tools, and the devloop tools when the project has devloop. It logs failed calls. | The agent over stdio, and the core in process. |
| Waiter | `src/wait.ts` | It holds a call until a review arrives or 45 seconds pass. `hoop wait` uses it in the background. | The store, by reading files. |
| Web | `src/web.ts`, `web/*` | It serves the JSON API and the pages, as plain JS modules with no build step. | The browser over HTTP on 127.0.0.1. |
| Page frame and statuses | `web/frame.js`, `web/status.js`, `web/icons.js` | Every page shares one frame and one label, color and icon per status. | The page modules in the browser. |
| Line kinds | `web/blocks.js` | One rule decides each line's kind, for the parser, the edit engine and the pages. | The parser, the edit engine and the pages. |
| Line renderer | `web/inline.js` | It shows lines as formatted text and maps every shown character back to the source. It draws table rows and hands diagrams to the diagram frame. | The page modules in the browser. |
| Outline | `web/outline.js` | It shows the sections as a tree that nests up to five levels under the title. | The review page in the browser. |
| Diagram frame | `web/diagram.js`, `web/diagram-frame.js` | It draws one diagram inside a sandboxed frame that can't touch the page. | The pages process, for the diagram library. |
| Conversations and hidden mode | `web/review.js`, `web/app.js`, `web/inline.js`, `web/app.css` | Resolved conversations collapse, and one page mode hides every comment. The line renderer marks what it draws. | The page modules in the browser. |
| Check runner | `src/checks.ts` | It runs the project's allowed check command on a markdown submission and reads its findings. Its result leads with a warning when the check didn't run. | The project's command, as a child process. |
| Check allow command | `src/allow.ts` | It shows a repository's check command, asks the person to confirm, and writes their allow entry. | The person in a terminal, and the person's settings file. |
| Findings panel | `web/checks.js` | It shows the latest checked revision's findings on the review page. | The review page in the browser. |
| Sign-in service | `src/signin.ts`, `web/signin.js` | It runs GitHub's device sign-in and names the login. It keeps each browser's sign-in for eight hours in the pages process's memory. The sign-in ID lives in the page's own storage and travels in a request header, not a cookie. Browsers share cookies across ports on one host. | GitHub over HTTPS, and the browser through a request header. |
| Audit trail view | `web/trail.js` | It shows every comment, agent approval and final approval of a review, with who and when. | It reads the review's stored events through the review's view. |
| Plan review hook | `plugins/hoop-plan`, `src/plan.ts` | It submits a plan when an agent leaves plan mode, waits, and lets the agent go on or stops it. | Claude Code through its hook interface, and `hoop plan-review`. |
| Change registry | `src/changes.ts` | It keeps each change request as written, with its type, kind, project, step history, checks, size choice, linked reviews and PRs. It holds the fold gate. | Repository files. |
| Review sequencer | `src/sequence.ts` | It keeps the PRD → HLD → LLD order, computes staleness, and holds the build gate. It writes no change rows into the tracker. | The change registry and repository files. |
| Change request page | `web/changes.js` | It lists every change by status and project, with its links, history and size flag. | The pages process's API. |
| Tracker service | `src/tracker.ts` | It reads markdown trackers as trees, with each item's block and project. It writes rows only, with a conflict check. | Repository files. |
| Tracker page | `web/tracker.js`, `web/tree.js` | It shows an item's block, its checklist count and missing blocks, and filters by project. | The pages process's API. |
| Wait, audit and CLI | `src/wait.ts`, `src/audit.ts`, `src/cli.ts` | They run `hoop wait`, write the audit log, and run `hoop audit` and every command. | The store and the audit log. |
| Shared helpers | `src/util.ts` | They hold errors, environment defaults, atomic writes, table rows, the hoop folder's settings, and each folder's repository identity. | Every component imports them. |
| Starter and pages process | `src/pages.ts` | Before a link, it checks the address and starts the pages process when nothing answers. The process restarts itself into current code, and stops when unused (FR-49, FR-51, FR-57). | The session registry and the address. |
| Session registry | `src/sessions.ts` | Each live `hoop mcp` session records its repository, release and install (FR-51). | Files under the hoop folder. |
| Versions | `src/version.ts` | It names an install's release and its code, from file sizes and times (FR-51). | The install's files. |
| Page start and notices | `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/tracker.js` | A page shows why it can't start, names its document's repository, and warns while its server is out of date (FR-52 to FR-55). | The pages process's API. |
| Schema publisher | `scripts/schemas.ts` | It writes the review and feedback formats as JSON Schema, and the README's field tables, from the contract. | The contract, at build time. |
| Repository tooling | `.githooks/`, `biome.json`, `scripts/comment-guard.ts`, `.github/` | Commit hooks, the linter and formatter, the comment guard and CI keep each change to the repository's practices. | Git and GitHub Actions. |
| Templates and standards | `plugins/devloop/skills/` | They give the shape of a PRD, an HLD and an LLD, and the rules reviewers apply, including what a PRD never holds. | Authors and reviewer agents read them as skills. |
| Persona agents | `plugins/devloop/agents/` | The owner and reviewer agents carry each document's altitude. | They follow the templates and standards. |
| Scoping and fold steps | `plugins/devloop/skills/` | They tell an author where requirements start and how a merged change lands in the project documents. | Authors follow them as skills. |
| Writing checker | `check_writing.py` | It finds a document's kind from its title and applies the rules for that kind. | It reads the document and the allowed names list as files, and prints findings. |
| Allowed names list | `docs/allowed-names.txt` | It lists the names a project's users type that look like code. | The writing checker reads it from the project's docs folder. |
| Fact map and script | `check_map.py` | The map records where each fact of an old document lands, and the script checks it. | The script reads the map and the new documents as files. |
| Practices skill | `plugins/devloop/skills/` | It checks a repository for the practices of FR-118 to FR-123. | An agent reads it as a skill. |
| Comparison | None | It compares hoop with similar review products and turns each gap into a queued change. | It feeds new change requests through intake. |

```mermaid flowchart TB   mcp[MCP server] --> ops[Operations]   cli[CLI] --> ops   ops --> core[Core]   core --> rules[Review rules]   core --> quote[Quote resolver]   core --> md[Markdown and section matcher]   core --> mat[Materializer]   mat --> edit[Edit engine]   core --> checks[Check runner]   core --> github[GitHub]   core --> reg[Change registry]   reg --> seq[Review sequencer]   core --> tracker[Tracker service]   core --> store[(Store)]   web[Web API] --> core   web --> signin[Sign-in service]   rules --> signin   pages[Pages in the browser] -->|HTTP on 127.0.0.1| web   pages --> frame[Diagram frame]   plan[Plan review hook] --> cli ```

items.title: Local channel
items.body: The agent submits. The reviewer comments on the page, and the page posts a feedback document. The agent reads it, or `hoop wait` or `hoop_wait` wakes it. Revisions repeat until the final approval, which writes `decisions/`.

items.title: GitHub channel
items.body: Submitting opens a PR (`hoop/<slug>`) with the JSON and a line-numbered `.md`. Each feedback read syncs the PR's reviews into the store again. Merge approves, and closing rejects.

items.title: An agent submits and waits
items.body:
```mermaid sequenceDiagram   participant A as Author agent   participant M as MCP server   participant C as Core   participant W as Waiter   A->>M: submit markdown   M->>C: submit   C-->>M: outcome, review to use next, check warning first   M-->>A: result   A->>M: wait   M->>W: hold for up to 45 seconds   W-->>A: the feedback, or "call again" ```

Failure: a wait that ends without a review says to call again. A superseded review's feedback names the review that replaced it.

items.title: A person gives the final approval
items.body:
```mermaid sequenceDiagram   participant B as Browser   participant P as Pages process   participant S as Sign-in service   participant G as GitHub   B->>P: Approve, with no sign-in yet   P->>S: start a device sign-in   S->>G: ask for a device code   G-->>S: code and address   S-->>B: show the code   B->>G: the person enters the code and confirms   S->>G: poll until confirmed   G-->>S: a token, used once to read the login   S-->>B: a sign-in for this browser, for eight hours   B->>P: Approve, with notes and the sign-in header   P->>P: record the final approval with the login ```

Failure: an expired, denied or unreachable sign-in records nothing, and the page says why. A verdict that arrives without the browser's sign-in is an agent's. An approve becomes an agent approval, and a request for changes becomes a comment.

items.title: An agent leaves plan mode
items.body:
```mermaid sequenceDiagram   participant CC as Claude Code   participant H as Plan review hook   participant M as hoop   CC->>H: the agent wants to leave plan mode, with its plan   H->>M: submit the plan   H->>M: wait for the final approval   alt approved     H-->>CC: allow   else changes requested     H-->>CC: stop, with the feedback   else no verdict in time     H-->>CC: stop, with the review's link   end ```

Failure: the hook fails closed. A missing `hoop`, a crash, output that isn't valid, or its own alarm each stop the agent with the reason.

items.title: A reviewer reads a structured document
items.body: The parser gives each section its heading level. The section matcher keeps each section's ID across revisions, first by heading and then by place. The page nests sections by level, groups a run of table lines into one table, and sends each diagram to its own sandboxed frame.

items.title: Materializing
items.body: Reviewer suggestions apply directly. The agent's proposals wait as tracked changes until accepted. Both go through the edit engine, so only the span changes. Each application is a new revision recorded in `applied.json`. A refused edit names the rule it broke.

items.title: A team tracks changes
items.body: The agent captures a request (`hoop cr create`), which lands in the repository as a change record. Each design document is submitted linked to its change. The sequencer refuses one whose predecessor isn't approved and current. Step moves go through the registry, which asks the sequencer before build and `gh` before fold. Each change keeps its kind, project, history and size choice in its own record. The change request page reads every record and shows it. The tracker holds no change rows, and its root items name their change.

items.title: An author writes and submits a PRD
items.body:
```mermaid sequenceDiagram   participant A as Author agent   participant C as Writing checker   participant H as hoop   participant R as Reviewer agents   A->>A: writes the PRD from the template   A->>C: checks the file   C-->>A: findings, each with what to write instead   A->>H: submits the PRD   H->>C: checks a copy, in the repository's folder   C-->>H: the same findings   H-->>A: the result, with the findings   R->>H: comment against the review standards ```

Failure: if the checker can't run, the submit result leads with a warning that the check didn't run. A check never stops a submit.

items.title: A change folds into the project documents
items.body: The fold steps move each requirement into the project PRD with its change tag. They move the design text into the project HLD and LLD with no change request names. The tests each requirement names land in the project LLD's test plan. The fold's documents go through the checker like any other. A fold that first moves a PRD to the five sections records a fact map, and the map script names each fact with no place.

items.title: Data and interfaces
items.body:
- Data: the store owns reviews, revisions, feedback, replies, proposals, applied edits and check   outcomes. The repository owns change records, trackers and decision files.
- Data: feedback gains each comment's scope, approval notes, whether a verdict is an agent's or a   person's, and the signed-in login. These are added fields, so stored reviews still load and the   format keeps its version (NFR-4).
- Data: a sign-in lives only in the pages process's memory, keyed by a random ID that the page   keeps in its own storage. No token is kept, and a restart of the pages process asks for a new   sign-in.
- Data: the templates, standards, agents and checker belong to devloop. The allowed names list, the   fact map and the project documents belong to the project.
- Core MCP tools: `hoop_submit` (markdown, and a decision document by its shape for two minor   versions), `hoop_submit_decision`, `hoop_feedback`, `hoop_wait`, `hoop_propose_edits`,   `hoop_reply` and `hoop_export`. The old name `hoop_submit_markdown` is still listed, marked as old.
- The devloop MCP tools are listed only in a project with devloop. They are `hoop_cr_create`, `hoop_cr_classify`,   `hoop_cr_step`, `hoop_cr_get`, `hoop_cr_link_pr`, `hoop_tracker_get` and `hoop_tracker_set`. Only   there do `hoop_submit` and `hoop_submit_decision` take `change: {cr, doc}`.
- Documents: `hoop/review@0` holds kind, channel, slug, title, tldr, and items with id, type,   title, body, check, choices, risk, depends_on and level. `hoop/feedback@0` holds the verdict,   comments, answers, resolved threads, viewed, reviewer and source.
- Feedback comments anchor by item, line and an optional range. A comment, reply or edit may name   quoted words in place of a line, and hoop resolves them before it stores anything.
- The feedback document's optional fields are `signed_in`, `unverified`, `agent_approval` and   `changes_requested_by_agent`. `schemas/review.schema.json` and `schemas/feedback.schema.json`   publish both formats.
- Anchors: item lines count from 1, and line 0 is a heading. Item `DOC` lines 1 and 2 are the   title and the TL;DR.
- HTTP pages, on 127.0.0.1 only: `GET /`, `GET /r/<id>`, `GET /tracker`, `GET /changes` and   `GET /vendor/mermaid.min.js`.
- HTTP reads: `GET /api/reviews`, `GET /api/reviews/<id>`, `GET /api/info`, `GET /api/trackers`,   `GET /api/tracker`, `GET /api/changes` and `GET /api/whoami`. The tracker and change routes take   `repo=<key>`.
- HTTP writes: `POST /api/reviews/<id>/feedback`, `POST /api/reviews/<id>/apply`,   `POST /api/reviews/<id>/edits/<edit>`, `POST /api/signin` and `GET /api/signin/<flow>`. The page   sends its sign-in in the `x-hoop-signin` header.
- `GET /api/info` gives `hoop`, `release`, `code`, `store`, `stale`, `pid` and `repos`, each   repository by name and key only (FR-53, FR-56). It no longer gives `repo`.
- A review's view gains `checks` without folder paths, `status_key`, `status_note`, `repo`,   `trail`, `renamed`, `superseded_by` and `decision_files`. Each item gains `blocks`.
- A submit result carries `outcome`, `next_review_id`, `cursor`, and `warnings` first when its   check didn't run. A result that gives a link carries `pages` when its pages can't be served.
- Files in the hoop folder: `reviews/<id>/{review,rev-N,feedback-N,replies,proposals,applied}.json`,   `reviews/<id>/checks-<revision>.json`, `audit.jsonl`, `config.json`, `sessions/<pid>.json` and   `plans/<session>.json`.
- The person's `config.json` holds the allowed checks, `signin: false` to turn the sign-in off, and   `github_client_id` to name their own OAuth App. No repository file can set these.
- Files in a repository: `decisions/<slug>.{json,md}`, `hoop.config.json` with its check command and   `devloop` setting, `docs/changes/CR-<n>-<slug>/{REQUEST.md, change.json}`,   `docs/changes/CLASSIFICATION.md` and `docs/TRACKER.md`.
- A change record holds its type, kind, project, steps, `history`, `size_choice`, linked reviews and   PRs. A history entry records a capture, pick-up, merge, split, drop or size choice.
- CLI: `hoop mcp`, `hoop serve`, `hoop wait <id> [--timeout s]`, `hoop audit [--since d] [--json]`,   `hoop allow-check`, `hoop plan-review`, and one command per operation (`hoop help`).
- `hoop submit` and `hoop submit-decision` are the submit commands, and `hoop submit-json` is the   old name. `hoop help` lists core and devloop commands in two groups, and every command runs in   any project.
- `hoop serve` runs in the foreground. With `HOOP_PAGES=background`, it is the pages process   (FR-49).
- Environment: `HOOP_HOME`, `HOOP_PORT`, `HOOP_REPO_DIR` and `HOOP_AUDIT`. `HOOP_CHROME`,   `HOOP_REQUIRE_BROWSER` and `HOOP_E2E_REPO` serve the tests and acceptance runs.
- `HOOP_PAGES` and `HOOP_PAGES_IDLE_MS` are internal to hoop and its tests (FR-49, FR-57).   `HOOP_BIN`, `HOOP_PLAN_ALARM` and `HOOP_PLAN_WAIT_SECONDS` tune the plan hook.
- External interfaces: GitHub's device sign-in over HTTPS, `gh api` for decision PRs, Claude Code's   hook interface, and GitHub Actions.
- The writing checker keeps its command line. It prints `path:line: message` for each finding, and   exits 0 with no findings and 1 with findings.

items.title: Cross-cutting concerns
items.body:
- Security: the local API refuses a foreign Host, a foreign Origin and non-JSON writes (NFR-1).   Reviewer comments reach the agent as data (NFR-2).
- Security: a check runs without a shell, with the document's path as its last argument. No request   from the page runs a check or waits for one, and no folder path reaches the page. This protects   NFR-13, NFR-15 and FR-41 to FR-44.
- Security: a check runs only when the person's own settings allow that exact command for that   folder (D-25). Only `hoop allow-check`, at a terminal, writes that entry (D-55).
- Security: a final approval proves that a person confirmed a GitHub login on GitHub (FR-83). It   stops an agent that uses only hoop's tools and pages.
- Security: an agent with a shell that works against the person isn't stopped. It could start a   sign-in and ask the person to confirm it, or edit the person's settings. devloop's rules forbid   each of these.
- Security: the sign-in ID travels in a custom header. A custom header from another origin needs a   preflight, which the server never grants. The page names who is signed in, and the audit log   records each sign-in.
- Security: a diagram draws in a sandboxed frame with no access to the page (NFR-20). The plan hook   fails closed. Turning the sign-in off marks each approval unverified (FR-84).
- Security: the pages never read file paths. The renderer builds markup only from escaped text and   a fixed set of tags, and links open only http and https addresses (FR-35).
- Performance: a 50-item review renders in under a second (NFR-3), and a 1000-line document in   under 200 milliseconds (NFR-12).
- Performance: the restart timer runs every two seconds, apart from any request. It reads session   entries and file sizes and times, so a page load never waits for it (NFR-16).
- Performance: the diagram library loads only on a page that has a diagram, which keeps NFR-19. A   wait holds at most 45 seconds (FR-66).
- Performance: the writing checker's rules are one pass over the text, about 40 milliseconds on   the project PRD. So the check stays well under NFR-24's one second.
- Reliability: only one process can bind the address, so two starters can't both serve (FR-49).   The pages process serves again when a restart fails (FR-51).
- Observability: every action and failure goes to the audit log (FR-23). It records sign-in, agent   approval, wait, quote refusal, edit refusal by rule, `check` and `pages_*` events.
- Observability: `hoop audit` reports time to verdict, revisions, edit acceptance, check counts and   the share of refused edits by rule (FR-24). The audit log also measures NFR-24.
- Testing: unit tests cover each rule, and browser tests cover every page state and a hostile   diagram. The page checks of NFR-11 run on every page.
- Testing: each rule about whether a review can change, and the thread lookup, is written once in   the review rules. The agent tools, their schemas and the commands match a recorded snapshot. Both   protect FR-31 and NFR-4.
- Testing: the acceptance runs cover the local page, documents, changes, two sessions in two   repositories, and the GitHub channel. CI runs the type check, the linter and the tests on each   supported Node version, and the browser tests (FR-122).
- Testing: the writing checker's own tests cover each rule, with a sample document for each kind of   finding. The map script proves NFR-22, and the project documents passing the checker prove   NFR-23.
- Deployment: hoop ships from source, and the starter runs the pages process from the session's   install. A contributor's install sets up the commit hooks, and installing hoop as a tool sets up   nothing (FR-119).
- Deployment: the plan hook ships as its own plugin in this repository's marketplace, which a person   turns on. devloop ships as a plugin too, and other projects get its rules when they update it.
- Deployment: a project turns devloop on in its `hoop.config.json`, and the next session lists   devloop's tools (FR-59). A project adds its allowed names list when its PRD first flags a name.

items.title: Alternatives and decisions
items.body:
- Alternative: a SQLite store, which loses because it needs a native module or Node 22+. JSON   files are enough without search.
- Alternative: a wrapper review agent, which loses because the code-review plugin already uses   fresh-context subagents.
- Alternative: GitHub only, which loses partial-text comments and a fast solo loop. GitHub is kept   for team review.
- Alternative: a separate headless review process, which loses because subagents and CI review are   simpler.
- Alternative: a free port for each session (FR-48), which loses because drafts in the browser   belong to an address. Moving port loses them.
- Alternative: every session stands by to take over the address (FR-49). This loses because each   needs a retry loop and a fallback, and the pages still stop with the last session.
- Alternative: tell agents from people by a header or a token on the machine. This loses, because   any agent with a shell can read or send it.
- Alternative: a passkey in the browser. The requester chose a GitHub identity instead.
- Alternative: draw diagrams in the page itself with the library's strict mode. This loses, because   one escape in the library would run inside the page that approves.
- Alternative: keep the old tool names unlisted. This loses, because an agent can only call a tool   the server lists.
- Alternative: keep change rows in the tracker and add the page beside it. This loses, because the   requester asked for change requests to leave the tracker.
- Alternative: do nothing about code in PRDs, and rely on reviewers. This loses, because the review   standard already forbade code and the project PRD still held 126 code spans.
- Alternative: hoop passes the document's file name to the checker. This loses, because it changes   hoop for no gain, and a title already names the kind.
- Alternative: flag every code span in a PRD. This loses, because code spans also hold literal text   and names users type, so it would give false findings.
- Alternative: one summary finding for a design document full of change request names. This loses,   because each finding sits on the line to fix.
- D-1: One contract over two channels (local page, GitHub PR), with the same feedback document.   Why: one path for the agent, and teams keep GitHub.
- D-2: JSON files in `~/.hoop` (was SQLite). Why: Node 18, no native modules, and nothing to query.
- D-3: The stdio MCP process also serves the page. Why: one command to set up. Replaced by D-29.
- D-4: Background `hoop wait` instead of a blocking tool call. Why: the session stays responsive.   Background waiting stays, and a bounded wait tool joins it under D-46.
- D-5: Merge approves and closing rejects on GitHub. Why: authors can't approve their own PRs, and   branch protection enforces team approvals.
- D-6: Decisions are code in `decisions/`. Why: git is the log, with no search tool.
- D-7: Comments anchor to whole lines or selected text locally, and to whole lines on GitHub.
- D-8: Materializing: reviewers apply exact suggestions, and the agent proposes span edits accepted   as tracked changes. Minimal rephrasing is enforced: text outside spans stays byte-identical.
- D-9: Headings scope their section, and title and TL;DR scope the document.
- D-10: A document line keeps its exact source text (U+2028 joins), so export is byte-identical.   Sections keep IDs by heading across revisions, and then by place under D-51.
- D-11: Every action and failure goes to an audit log for the improvement loop.
- D-12 (FR-17): Documents parsed from a `#` title keep blank lines in section bodies and are marked   `spacing: "exact"`. Documents without the marker (stored before exact spacing, or untitled) keep   the one-blank-line layout. Why: byte-identical export without breaking stored reviews.
- D-13 (FR-25, FR-29): The repository is the source of truth for changes and trackers, and hoop's   store keeps reviews. Why: visible and diffable in the repository.
- D-14 (FR-27, FR-28): Gates live in hoop, not in the skill, so any agent is held to them.
- D-15 (FR-27): Staleness is computed from approval times, not stored.
- D-16 (FR-31): Terminal commands mirror the agent tools one to one, from one operations table.   Old names stay as aliases under D-45, and `hoop allow-check` is a terminal-only command under D-55.
- D-17 (FR-26): Classification corrections are recorded in the repository and read by devloop.
- D-18 (FR-31, NFR-4): The core stays the single entry point and only coordinates. The review rules   own every check that a review can change, and the thread lookup, each written once.
- D-19 (FR-36, FR-37): The pages format each line themselves and keep a map to source offsets, so   comments anchor to source text on formatted lines.
- D-20 (FR-35): The server decides each line's kind once, in one shared module, and the edit engine   uses it too.
- D-21 (FR-32, FR-33): The server gives each review a status key and a repository identity. The   pages only name each status, and they never read file paths.
- D-22 (NFR-11): Icons are inline SVG and fonts come from the system, so the pages fetch nothing.
- D-23 (FR-39): An automatic TL;DR shows once, as the first paragraph. A document with its own   TL;DR still shows it first, and D-9 still holds.
- D-24 (FR-41, FR-43): The project's command holds the writing rules, and hoop only runs it and   reads its `path:line: message` output. Exit 0 means no findings, and exit 1 means findings. Any   other code means the check didn't run.
- D-25 (FR-41): A check runs only when the user's own config allows that exact command for that   folder. hoop can't stop an agent that edits that config, so devloop's rules forbid it. The same   rule covers the sign-in opt out and starting a sign-in.
- D-26 (FR-43): A check never blocks a submission. devloop's document review stays the strict layer.
- D-27 (FR-46): The page holds which threads are open and whether comments are hidden in   memory only, so each visit starts with every comment shown.
- D-28 (FR-46): Hiding comments is one page mode applied by styles, keyed on a `data-comment`   marker. Later renderers inherit it by marking what they draw.
- D-29 (FR-49): The pages run in one background process that no session owns. Why: drafts, links   and the guide depend on one address, and reviews outlive sessions.
- D-30 (NFR-14, FR-57): Only the pages process's own timer can stop or restart it, and no request   can. Only same-site requests count as use. Why: a web page can send plain requests to the   address, so no route is added to defend.
- D-31 (FR-51): A server serves the page files it started with. Why: a server's pages must match   its routes.
- D-32 (FR-51): Out of date means the newest release a live session's install holds differs from   the server's, or its own files changed. Why: rollbacks happen, and two installs of one release   must not restart each other.
- D-33 (2026-10-20): The checker learns a document's kind from its title. Context: hoop checks a   temporary copy whose name says nothing (FR-117). Consequences: every template's title names its   kind.
- D-34 (2026-10-20): The code rule flags only what text shows reliably. Those are file paths, source   and test file names, function calls and web routes. Context: plain words that name code can't be   told from product words (FR-108). Consequences: the review standards cover the rest.
- D-35 (2026-10-20): A PRD in the old shape gets one finding until it moves to the five sections.   Context: other projects would otherwise see dozens of findings at once (FR-115). Consequences: the   code and tag rules apply only to a PRD in the new shape.
- D-36 (2026-10-20): A design document's title and status line may name a change request. Context:   they identify the document, and the rule is about its design text (FR-109). Consequences: the   rule skips those two lines.
- D-37 (2026-10-20): The fact map's format and its script ship in devloop, and the fold steps use   them. Context: every project with documents under the old rules must move them once, and NFR-22   needs the same proof there. Consequences: hoop's own map is the first one.
- D-38 (2026-10-20): The comparison runs before the rewrite, and its gaps go through intake.   Context: the PRD's open questions must name each gap's change request (FR-113). Consequences:   intake checks each new request against the queue for overlaps.
- D-39 (2026-10-20): A change's requirements take the next free project IDs when it is scoped. A   change to an existing requirement uses its project ID. Context: a fold used to renumber them, so a   design ID would mean another requirement (FR-110).   Consequences: the scoping step reads the project PRD and every queued change's PRD for the next   free ID. A fold checks that no ID clashes.
- D-40 (2026-10-20): A fold into a project PRD in the old shape first moves that PRD to the five   sections, with a fact map. Context: a fold must place requirements in sections the old PRD lacks   (FR-111, FR-112). Consequences: a project moves its PRD once, at its next fold. Its HLD and LLD   lose their change request names in the same fold.
- D-41 (2026-10-20): An author runs the check the project configures for hoop, when there is one,   and the checker from devloop otherwise. Context: FR-117 needs the same findings from the file and   from a submit. Consequences: the writing style skill says so.
- D-42 (2026-10-20): A file named for its kind, whose title doesn't name that kind, gets one   finding. Context: without it, a missing kind turns off the new rules with no sign (FR-117).   Consequences: on submit, hoop's copy has no such name, so this finding shows only on the author's   run.
- D-43 (2026-10-20): The checker looks for the allowed names list from the document's folder   upward, and then from its working folder upward. Context: an author checks the file in the   project, and hoop checks a copy from the project's folder (FR-116). Consequences: both runs find   the same list.
- D-44 (2026-10-20): Each operation is marked core or devloop, and the MCP server lists devloop   tools only in a project with devloop. A project has devloop when its config says so or it holds   change requests. Context: FR-58, FR-59 and FR-141. Consequences: the terminal keeps every command.
- D-45 (2026-10-20): `hoop_submit` takes markdown and also accepts a decision document by its   shape, for the next two minor versions. The old names are aliases in the operations table.   Context: FR-61 and FR-62. Consequences: the recorded interface changes once, and the changelog   says the aliases go after two minor versions.
- D-46 (2026-10-20): Waiting is a core operation that holds for at most 45 seconds and returns.   Context: FR-66 and the client's 60 second limit. Consequences: background waiting stays as it   is.
- D-47 (2026-10-20): A quote resolves to a line, and a range inside it, before the feedback is   stored. Context: FR-71. Consequences: stored feedback keeps line anchors, so both channels and   stored reviews work unchanged.
- D-48 (2026-10-20): Only a browser sign-in marks a person. A verdict without it counts as an   agent's. Context: FR-81 to FR-84 and FR-143. Consequences: the page posts verdicts with the   browser's sign-in, and agents keep posting comments.
- D-49 (2026-10-20): A sign-in lives only in the pages process's memory, for eight hours, and the   GitHub token is dropped after reading the login. Context: NFR-5 and FR-143. Consequences: a   restart of the pages process asks the person to sign in again.
- D-50 (2026-10-20): A person's own settings can turn the sign-in off or name their own OAuth App,   and no repository setting can. Context: FR-84 and FR-144. Consequences: approvals without a   sign-in carry an unverified mark everywhere.
- D-51 (2026-10-20): A section keeps its ID by heading first. A section left unmatched keeps the ID   of the old section at the same level, under the same parent, in the same place. Context: FR-78   and FR-142.
- D-51 consequences: the rule that IDs follow headings widens, and stored reviews keep their IDs.   Section IDs stay flat as sections nest. A section matched by place shows that its heading was   renamed, so a reviewer sees its comments moved.
- D-52 (2026-10-20): Each table line stays one commentable line, and the page groups a run of them   into one table. Context: FR-79. Consequences: anchors and edits on table rows work as before.
- D-53 (2026-10-20): Each diagram draws in a sandboxed frame with no same origin access, from a   copy of the library that the pages process serves. Context: FR-80 and NFR-20.
- D-53 consequences: the frame's content policy allows only the library's own file, and no popups,   forms or navigation. A diagram can't run script in the page or make a request, and pages without   diagrams load no library.
- D-54 (2026-10-20): The plan review hook ships as its own plugin, which uses hoop's commands and   fails closed. Context: FR-87 and FR-145. Consequences: a person turns it on by installing it.
- D-55 (2026-10-20): Allowing a check is a terminal command that needs a person at a terminal, and   isn't an agent tool. Context: FR-70 and FR-140. Consequences: an agent can't allow a check   through hoop, and devloop's rule against editing the settings stays.
- D-56 (2026-10-20): A change's record in the repository holds its kind, project, history and size   choice. Context: FR-94 to FR-98. Consequences: the change request page only reads, and every   change to a record goes through a devloop operation.
- D-57 (2026-10-20): The tracker keeps work items only, and a root item names its change. Context:   FR-93. Consequences: the sequencer writes no change rows.
- D-58 (2026-10-20): The contract is the one source for the JSON Schema files and the README's   field tables, and a test fails when they drift. Context: FR-127. Consequences: a field change   regenerates both.
- D-59 (2026-10-20): Commit hooks are plain git hooks kept in the repository, set up only in a   contributor's clone, and Biome lints and formats. Context: FR-119 to FR-122. Consequences:   installing hoop as a tool sets up nothing.
- D-60 (2026-10-20): An agent approval is stored as a comment verdict with an agent approval   mark. Context: older readers treat a stored approval as final (FR-82). Consequences: an older   hoop, the GitHub status rule and devloop's agents never mistake it for a final approval.
- D-61 (2026-10-20): The plan hook keeps one review for each session's plan. A retry finds it,   revises it when the plan changed, and goes on when its latest revision is approved.
- D-61 continued: a plan review writes no decision files. Context: FR-87 and FR-145. Consequences:   a person who approves late approves once, and the stop message says to approve and then ask the   agent to go on.
- D-62 (2026-10-20): hoop writes no change rows, and still reads trackers that hold them. The   tracker page shows such rows apart, and devloop's fold step removes them. Context: FR-93 in other   repositories. Consequences: an older hoop that writes a change row is harmless.
- D-63 (2026-10-20): A restart of the pages process drops every sign-in, and the person signs in   again. Context: handing sign-ins to the new process would need them outside memory, where an   agent could read them (FR-143). Consequences: a person signs in again after an update.
- D-64 (2026-10-20): A session reads whether its project has devloop when it starts. devloop's   setup says to start a new session. Context: an MCP tool list is fixed for a session (FR-59).   Consequences: turning devloop on takes effect in the next session.
- D-65 (2026-10-20): A project is a label on changes and tracker items inside a repository. It   defaults to the repository's name. A review takes its change's project, or its repository's.   Context: FR-96 and FR-97. Consequences: filters work the same for reviews, changes and items.
- D-66 (2026-10-20): An unverified final approval unlocks what any final approval unlocks, and   carries its mark into every place that shows it. Context: FR-84. Consequences: devloop reports   an unverified approval when it reaches a gate.

items.title: Traceability and risks
items.body:
| Requirement | Components |
|---|---|
| FR-1, FR-2, NFR-4 | Contract, core, store, schema publisher. |
| FR-3, FR-4, FR-6, FR-7, FR-19 | Web, line renderer, outline, review rules. |
| FR-5, FR-8, FR-11 | Core, waiter, MCP server, GitHub. |

| NFR-1, NFR-2 | Web, core. |

| FR-58, FR-59, FR-60, FR-141 | Operations, MCP server, project settings. |
| FR-61, FR-62, FR-63, FR-64, FR-65 | Operations, core, review page. |
| FR-66, FR-67, FR-139 | Waiter. |
| FR-68, FR-69 | Check runner, findings panel. |
| FR-70, FR-140 | Check allow command. |
| FR-71, FR-72, FR-136 | Quote resolver, core. |

| FR-74, FR-75 | Line renderer, review page. |
| FR-76, FR-77 | Outline, line renderer, contract. |

| FR-79 | Line renderer. |
| FR-80, FR-134, FR-138, NFR-19, NFR-20 | Diagram frame, line renderer. |
| FR-81, FR-82, FR-83, FR-84, FR-85, FR-143, FR-144 | Review rules, sign-in service. |
| FR-86 | Audit trail view. |

| NFR-23 | Writing checker, project documents, templates and standards. |
| NFR-24 | Writing checker. |

- Risk: rubber-stamping moves to the browser. It is mitigated by a summary first (a document's own   TL;DR, or its first paragraph under D-23), and risk shown per item.
- Risk: a document could inject markup into the page. The renderer builds markup only from escaped   text and a fixed set of tags, and links open only http and https addresses (FR-35).
- Risk: a new kind of comment element without the `data-comment` marker stays visible when comments   are hidden. The page checks run with comments hidden, and a browser test looks for comment text   (FR-46).
- Risk: a cloned repository's config could run code on submit. Only the user's own allow entry lets   a command run, and a changed command needs a new entry (FR-41).
- Risk: an allow entry binds the command, not the scripts it runs, so a pull can change such a   script. A slow check also adds up to ten seconds to a submit (FR-41, FR-43).
- Risk: a selection maps to the wrong source text on a formatted line. Unit tests check the source   map, and browser tests check selections inside code, bold text and links (FR-36).
- Risk: prompt injection through comments, mitigated by returning feedback as data (NFR-2).
- Risk: the local API is reachable from web pages, mitigated by Host, Origin and content-type   checks (NFR-1).
- Risk: edits drift onto other text, mitigated by binding proposals to their line's exact text.
- Risk: hand edits to a tracker while hoop writes it. Row-only writes refuse a file that changed   since it was read.
- Risk: approvals in the same millisecond compare as equal, so the later document isn't marked   stale.
- Risk: a session entry names the command a restart runs. Only small regular files that the user   owns count, and the audit log records the release and code that each restart runs (FR-51).
- Risk: a crashed session leaves its registry entry. An entry counts only while its process runs,   with the same start time, and only when the user owns it (FR-51).
- Risk: two sessions start the pages process at once. Only one can bind, and the other records that   it never started (FR-49).
- Risk: an update is read half written. The successor may fail to start, so the old process serves   again and marks itself out of date (FR-51).
- Risk: an agent reads the browser's sign-in from the browser's own files. It is mitigated by   keeping the sign-in in memory with an eight hour limit, and the security policy names the risk.
- Risk: the OAuth App is missing or unreachable. It is mitigated by a sign-in page that names the   problem, the person's own app and the opt out (FR-133, FR-144).
- Risk: the diagram library is large. It is mitigated by loading it only on pages with a diagram.
- Risk: matching a renamed heading by place picks the wrong section when sections move and are   renamed at once. It is mitigated by matching by heading first, and by tests for moves.
- Risk: the code rule flags a name users type, in a project with no list. It is mitigated by the   finding's message, which says to add the name to the allowed names list.
- Risk: a fold loses a fact when a document moves to the new rules. It is mitigated by the fact map   and its script, and by review as a diff in hoop.
- Risk: other projects see new findings after they update devloop. It is mitigated by D-35's single   finding for an old PRD, D-40's move at the next fold, and the version notes.

items.title: Glossary
items.body:
- Agent approval: an approval that records an agent's view and never freezes a review.
- Final approval: the approval that freezes a review, made in a signed-in browser.
- Sign-in: a browser's proof, for eight hours, that a person confirmed a GitHub login.
- Devloop layer: the change request and tracker tools that a project turns on.
- Project: a label on changes and tracker items inside a repository.
- Kind: whether a document is a PRD, an HLD or an LLD, as its title names it.
- Change tag: the closing part of a requirement that names the change requests that changed it.
- Fact map: the table of each fact in an old project document and its new place.
